propositions: Review-kernel findings carry an impact-only severity label that does not correlate with the authoritative priority metric (validity × impact), creating inconsistency where high-impact/low-validity findings appear critical but rank below major-severity findings.

The severity label is frequently misread as the gate decision signal when priority is the actual source of truth, and field translation via _KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY causes the same finding to surface with different severity (INFO vs MEDIUM) across identical runs when only impact drifts.

Review-kernel must stop stamping severity onto findings and instead emit priority (float) and decision (block/advisory) consistently; all consumers (aggregation, Gerrit review-bot, CLI renderers, workflow gates) must migrate to the new schema.

The shared SEVERITIES vocabulary in findings.py must remain intact for non-review-kernel producers (completion-verification cluster, spec_scan.py) that do not compute priority/validity/impact and are unaffected by this migration.
CLI renderers and the Gerrit comment must surface review-kernel-sourced findings as blocking/advisory, never as severity words, while preserving severity rendering for findings from other producers.
